recommendations.regimenLabel: Anticoagulation reversal + ICP/seizure control + neurosurgical referral
steps: Surgical evacuation (burr hole for chronic, craniotomy for acute) if symptomatic/large with mass effect.
Small asymptomatic collections: observe with repeat imaging.

drugRefs.why: Rapid reversal of vitamin-K-antagonist anticoagulation in intracranial haemorrhage; faster than FFP.
Given with PCC to sustain reversal of warfarin as PCC effect wanes.
Specific reversal agent for dabigatran-associated intracranial bleeding.

drugRefs.freq: as needed for surges in ICP
drugRefs.why: Reduces raised intracranial pressure from mass effect as a temporising measure.
Manages/prevents post-haemorrhage seizures; favourable interaction profile.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Traumatic Brain Injury / Intracranial Haemorrhage
Neurocritical Care Society — Reversal of Antithrombotics in Intracranial Haemorrhage
Brain Trauma Foundation Guidelines for the Management of Severe TBI

confirm: Headache, fluctuating consciousness or cognitive decline, sometimes after (minor) trauma — esp. elderly/anticoagulated. CT shows crescentic collection.
